author: Mod Ash
quote: Orders included: - Must finish the series. - Must tidy off Kennith's story. - You can't have the GFX budget for child-sized animations for Kennith. - Must tidy off some penguin plot point... - ... but cannot require all the other quests involved in that. - Must be about Dungeoneering because that'd be good for marketing. - Must not entail challenging combat because high-level quests exclude too many players. Some of that's self-contradictory, and you can see how you wind up with (1) Kennith becoming an adult instantly, which is at least funny, (2) a final fight with Mother Mallum where she doesn't fight, and (3) random penguin references that go nowhere.

author: Mod Ash
quote: And there's no way we'd backport Salt in the Wound as a Slug finale either. Even if we had Kennith's Concerns and Daemonheim, no-one would likely thank us for that particular quest. Its dev was very frustrated with the design constraints he was told to work under, and he quit soon after.

quote: Well we've talked before about how many "runes" are the different resonances - i.e. colours, flavours, wavelengths - of anima, i.e. the magical energy of the elder gods. Meanwhile the "ancient elements" appear to be the different resonances of the magical energy of erebus.

author: Mod Jack
quote: Yes. I don't want to say "this is canon" because it's not even implied. But it's sort of... indirectly implied if you think about it in a meta way. There's an obvious thematic association between the ancient elements. Therefore we can assume that if one came from erebus, they all probably did. But that's not the same thing as "canonically they all came from erebus".
